notes: Pencil 17. The author enlarges the category by open inclusions, described as “bouchage de trous”, and considers maps extending to finite ramified maps of completed surfaces. The source writes comp. clos, not complexes. In (23) the forked, retraced target is Y. In the boundary definition the ink instead clearly writes T = Y-hat minus T, where the intended definition would be T = Y-hat minus Y. The last paragraph has a clear C where the surrounding set notation would require S. These two slips are retained. With the intended boundary definition, the containment (25) expresses that points above the omitted target boundary must be omitted from X; extra omitted source points can lie over Y and carry ramification of the completed map. The local phenomenon can be checked with z mapping to z squared: remove 0 from the source but keep 0 in the target. The restricted map is étale while its extension ramifies at the removed source point. No assertion about the full enlarged category is proved here.

checks.statement: With T = Y-hat minus Y and X mapping into Y, the inverse image of T lies in S = X-hat minus X.
checks.outcome: If a point above T belonged to X, its image under the restricted map would lie outside Y, a contradiction.

checks.statement: A completed finite map can ramify at an omitted source point whose image is not omitted from the target.
checks.outcome: Over characteristic zero, z squared from C-star to C has nonzero derivative on its source; the extension to projective lines ramifies at 0, which is omitted only from the source. This checks the local mechanism, not a general theorem about the proposed category.
